title: Calendar interval is required; distance and hours are optional
custom_preconds:
1. You are signed in as an Owner/Admin, or a user with "Settings Service" enabled, on the build under test. The Maintenance Reminders feature is on (it ships behind the maintenance_reminders flag).
  2. A schedule open in the editor with the service form ready. Seed it:
  3. ↳ Settings > Maintenance > New schedule (or open an existing schedule and Edit).
  4. ↳ Click Add service to open the blank service form.
  5. Leave "is this compliance" off (a routine service).
custom_steps:
1. Look at the calendar interval control and try to untick it (hover its checkbox).
  2. Tick Distance, then Engine hours, and watch the interval rows appear.
  3. Try to Save with the calendar interval left empty.
  4. Save a service with no additional trigger selected.
  5. Select Distance and Engine hours together and count the calendar rows.
custom_expected:
Expected results

  • The calendar interval is always present, always editable and required - a ticked checkbox that cannot be unticked, with a hover explaining every service carries a calendar interval.
  • Distance and Engine hours are optional additional triggers; ticking each reveals its own interval row.
  • A service cannot be saved with the calendar interval empty; a service with calendar only (no additional trigger) saves fine.
  • Distance and Engine hours selected together still produce one calendar row, not two.

Source — where this behaviour comes from
Epic SV-3780; story SV-10559 (S2, Add a routine service to a schedule); Chunk 1 MR spec (Confluence 886931488), S2; read 29 Sep 2026. Source-verified 29 September 2026; not yet build-verified.

Exact quotes from the source (for reproducibility)

  • S2-R4: “The calendar interval will always be present, always editable, and required. It shows as a ticked checkbox that cannot be unticked, with a hover explaining that every service carries a calendar interval”
  • S2-R5: “Distance and engine hours will be optional additional triggers, each revealing its own interval row when selected”
  • S2-N1: “A service cannot be saved with the calendar interval empty”
  • S2-N3: “Selecting no additional trigger is valid. Calendar alone is a complete service”
  • S2-E1: “Distance and engine hours selected together still produce one calendar row, not two”
